question: What historical fish evidence does the 2014 Laguna de Bay two-cove fish-trap study provide, and are its results reusable in Bangwit?

bibliography.citation: Cuvin-Aralar, M. L. A. (2014). Fish biodiversity and incidence of invasive fish species in an aquaculture and non-aquaculture site in Laguna de Bay, Philippines. In C. Biscarini, A. Pierleoni, & L. Naselli-Flores (Eds.), Lakes: The Mirrors of the Earth. Balancing Ecosystem and Human Wellbeing. Proceedings of the 15th World Lake Conference, Vol. 2, pp. 53-57. Science4Press.

sites.sourceDescription: Open fishery area with no aquaculture structures
Aquaculture site with cages for Nile tilapia, bighead carp, and giant freshwater prawn

studyAssessment.method: Bamboo-pole and net fish traps were installed at both coves and harvested every two weeks. The authors determined biomass and counts of each species and compared community indices and catch per unit effort.
studyAssessment.reportedFindings: The authors report no significant difference in species richness between the two sites, higher diversity and evenness at the open-fishery West Cove, and higher fishery biomass at the aquaculture East Cove. These are study-specific historical comparisons, not a causal lake-wide result.
studyAssessment.samplingInterruption: The paper reports that a water-hyacinth bloom disrupted the West Cove trap from September through December 2013, limiting comparability across the full period.
studyAssessment.scopeAndResolution: The paper concerns two adjacent local sites and a one-year historical sampling period. Its locator figure is not georeferenced for this project. This review did not transcribe the source tables or figures into a species-by-date event dataset; the study is not a complete Laguna de Bay checklist, present-day occurrence layer, or lake-wide fishery assessment.

accessAndRights.officialMetadata: The SEAFDEC/AQD repository provides the title, author, year, abstract, and suggested citation.
accessAndRights.fullTextAccess: The proceedings text was reviewed online through an institutional repository reader and cross-checked against a second repository copy. No local PDF was downloaded or retained.
accessAndRights.proceedingsRightsNotice: The proceedings front matter states Copyright © 2014 by Umbria Scientific Meeting Association (USMA2007), All rights reserved.
accessAndRights.itemSpecificLicense: No open license or separate permission for this paper, its tables, or its figures was identified.
accessAndRights.decision: Retain citation and concise research notes only. Do not reproduce the paper, tables, figures, or source-derived fish rows in the app unless item-specific reuse is authorized.

decision.reason: The study is useful as dated, localized historical evidence, but its two-cove design cannot stand for the whole lake, the record-level species/site/date crosswalk has not been prepared, and the proceedings state all rights reserved with no separate reuse permission found.

nextAction: Seek an authorized species-by-date/site extract and item-specific reuse terms from the author or rights holder, or prioritize an independently reusable lake-wide or multi-site fish survey. Keep this study research-only and do not infer current fish presence, catchability, safety, legality, diet, or bait advice.
